studies.title: Eliyahu and Elisha: The Covenant Succession Pattern
studies.summary: Nine direct narrative parallels across Melakhim Aleph and Melakhim Bet, grounded verse by verse, plus the structural asymmetry (a double portion of spirit) that the text itself names as the reason Elisha's miracle count runs higher.

sections.heading: Multiplying provision for a widow in need
sections.body: Eliyahu: Melakhim Aleph 17:8-16 (1 Kings 17:8-16) — the jar of flour and jug of oil that don't run out, for the widow of Tzarefat, sustaining her through famine. Elisha: Melakhim Bet 4:1-7 (2 Kings 4:1-7) — the oil that fills every borrowed vessel, for a prophet's widow, paying off a debt and saving her sons from slavery. Same miracle-shape (oil multiplied from near-nothing), different crisis (famine vs. debt-slavery) and different outcome (ongoing sustenance vs. one-time payoff).

sections.heading: Raising a dead son
sections.body: Eliyahu: Melakhim Aleph 17:17-24 (1 Kings 17:17-24) — the Tzarefat widow's son, stretched over three times, the boy's life returning. Elisha: Melakhim Bet 4:18-37 (2 Kings 4:18-37) — the Shunammite's son, Elisha lying on him mouth-to-mouth, the child sneezing seven times and opening his eyes. Eliyahu's one widow receives both this miracle and the oil miracle; Elisha splits the two miracle-types across two different women.

sections.heading: Parting the Jordan with the mantle — same spot, reversed
sections.body: Eliyahu: Melakhim Bet 2:8 (2 Kings 2:8) — rolls up his cloak, strikes the water, crosses on dry ground with Elisha, heading away from Yisra'EL. Elisha: Melakhim Bet 2:14 (2 Kings 2:14) — picks up the fallen cloak, strikes the same water at the same crossing, asking, Where is YHWH, the Creator of Eliyahu? — crosses back alone. The text stages this as a deliberate echo: same object, same river, same action, read by the sons of the prophets watching as proof the spirit of Eliyahu rests on Elisha (2:15).

sections.heading: Supernatural judgment on open mockery or defiance
sections.body: Eliyahu: Melakhim Bet 1:9-12 (2 Kings 1:9-12) — fire from heaven consumes two captains of fifty sent by Akhazyahu; the third, who humbles himself, is spared. Elisha: Melakhim Bet 2:23-24 (2 Kings 2:23-24) — curses mocking boys at Beit-El in YHWH's name; two she-bears maul forty-two of them. Both episodes sit at the hinge of a transition: Eliyahu's is his last recorded act before the whirlwind (ch.2 follows immediately); Elisha's is his first recorded act after receiving the mantle.

sections.heading: Eliyahu's three-part commission, fulfilled through Elisha
sections.body: Melakhim Aleph 19:15-17 (1 Kings 19:15-17) — at Khorev, YHWH tells Eliyahu to anoint Khaza'el over Aram, Yehu over Yisra'EL, and Elisha as his own prophetic successor. Elisha personally carries out the Khaza'el commission: Melakhim Bet 8:7-15 (2 Kings 8:7-15), weeping as he foresees what Khaza'el will do. Elisha delegates the Yehu commission to a servant-prophet: Melakhim Bet 9:1-10 (2 Kings 9:1-10). A single multi-generational commission, worked out through Elisha rather than Eliyahu himself.

sections.heading: Judgment on the house of Akhav, pronounced then executed
sections.body: Eliyahu pronounces it: Melakhim Aleph 21 (1 Kings 21), after Navot's murder. It lands a generation later through Elisha's anointed instrument, Yehu: Melakhim Bet 9-10 (2 Kings 9-10).

sections.heading: Covenant miracle reaching a hostile nation's own person
sections.body: Eliyahu: the Tzarefat widow — a Tzidonian woman in Izevel's home territory (Melakhim Aleph 17:9 / 1 Kings 17:9). Elisha: Na'aman — an Aramean army commander, healed of leprosy by dipping seven times in the Yarden (Melakhim Bet 5:1-14 / 2 Kings 5:1-14), who then confesses there is no Creator in all the earth but in Yisra'EL (5:15).

sections.heading: Death, and power continuing past it — asymmetric, not parallel
sections.body: Eliyahu never dies: taken up by a whirlwind, one of only two recorded translations without death in the covenant canon (the other being Khanokh, Bereshit 5:24). Elisha dies an ordinary death and is buried (Melakhim Bet 13:20 / 2 Kings 13:20) — but a corpse thrown into his grave revives on touching his bones (13:21): the covenant life that flowed through Elisha during his ministry overflows the boundary of his death — power persisting through death rather than escaping it.

sections.heading: The same cry, a generation apart
sections.body: Elisha cries, My father, my father — the chariots of Yisra'EL and its horsemen, as Eliyahu is taken (Melakhim Bet 2:12 / 2 Kings 2:12). King Yo'ash weeps the identical words at Elisha's own deathbed (Melakhim Bet 13:14 / 2 Kings 13:14) — the same cry recurring, the covenant succession of the prophetic word echoing through the generations.

sections.heading: The structural asymmetry underneath all of it
sections.body: Elisha himself requests it directly: let there be a double portion of your spirit on me (Melakhim Bet 2:9 / 2 Kings 2:9). Consistent with that request, Elisha's narrated miracle count runs noticeably higher than Eliyahu's across these volumes — roughly twice as many individual wonders. Eliyahu's own calling is never narrated — he appears abruptly, without introduction, standing before Akhav. Elisha's calling, by contrast, is fully staged: found plowing, the cloak thrown over him, his explicit response (Melakhim Aleph 19:19-21 / 1 Kings 19:19-21).
